A multi-agent generator-evaluator harness for Claude Code and Codex - it audits, fixes, builds, and hardens a repo in gated loops until adversarial judges sign off.

--- Most AI coding loops pass tests and call it done. gauntlet doesn't trust that. It separates the agent that produces work from the agents that judge it, runs every gate exactly as CI would, and demands proof that tests can actually fail - not just that they currently pass. > *The gate is CI, verbatim. The evaluator is never the generator. Tests must prove they can fail.*

The gated generator → evaluator loop. Each arrow is a checkpoint, not a suggestion.

--- ## What's Inside | Mechanism | What It Does | |-----------|-------------| | **Generator ≠ Evaluator** | Producers never grade their own work. Every medium+ finding gets 2 independent skeptics prompted to REFUTE (a 3rd breaks a split). | | **The gate is CI, verbatim** | No filtered subsets, no "just the new tests." Full suite at every major checkpoint - because a modified test class once hid the only red assertion. | | **Prove tests can fail** | Every regression test must go red with the fix stashed. A test that passes on broken code is not coverage. | | **File ownership for parallel agents** | Concurrent agents get disjoint file lists. No mid-flight commits. No partial-edit sweeps. | | **Harness state in `.harness/`** | `feature-list.json` (goal tracking with verification contracts) + `progress.md` (append-only iteration log). Git-excluded, never stale. | | **Final signoff panel** | Three read-only reviewers - MAINTAINER, ADOPTER, RELEASER - each empowered to block with "I would not ship this." | | **Six-phase sequence (A → F)** | Recon → Audit → Fix → Build → Docs → Final loop. Structured, gated, repeatable. | | **Docs honesty** | Every claim verified against current code. No invented numbers. Performance figures trace to committed docs or output you generated. | ---
``` ┌─────────────┐ │ ◆ ◆ │ │ │ ≠ │ │ │ GEN EVAL │ │PRODUCER JUDGE│ └─────────────┘ ``` **Generator ≠ Evaluator**

--- ## Installation ### Claude Code one-liner (default) ```bash curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vivekptnk/gauntlet/main/install.sh | bash ``` The installer copies the skill bundle to `~/.claude/skills/gauntlet/` and verifies Claude Code can find it. ### Codex one-liner ```bash curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vivekptnk/gauntlet/main/install.sh | bash -s -- --codex ``` The Codex installer target copies the same skill bundle to `${CODEX_HOME:-$HOME/.codex}/skills/gauntlet/` and verifies the frontmatter Codex uses to discover skills. ### Git clone + install ```bash git clone https://github.com/vivekptnk/gauntlet.git cd gauntlet ./install.sh # Claude Code ./install.sh --codex # Codex ``` ### Manual copy ```bash mkdir -p ~/.claude/skills/gauntlet cp -R skills/gauntlet/. ~/.claude/skills/gauntlet/ mkdir -p "${CODEX_HOME:-$HOME/.codex}/skills/gauntlet" cp -R skills/gauntlet/. "${CODEX_HOME:-$HOME/.codex}/skills/gauntlet/" ``` ### Zero-install: Bootstrap prompt No skill infrastructure needed. Open `BOOTSTRAP-PROMPT.md`, fill the `` slot, and paste the whole thing into a fresh Claude Code or Codex session in your target repo. The orchestrator self-organizes from there. --- ### Invoking the harness Once installed, from any Claude Code session in your repo: ``` /gauntlet ``` Or with project-specific goals: ``` /gauntlet ship the auth module, harden the CI, and polish the README to portfolio grade ``` In Codex, ask for the skill by name from inside your repo: ``` Use gauntlet to ship the auth module, harden the CI, and polish the README to portfolio grade ``` The orchestrator reads your repo, writes `.harness/`, and proceeds through all six phases without asking permission between them. For a non-mutating plan: ``` /gauntlet --dry-run ship the auth module ``` Or in Codex: ``` Use gauntlet --dry-run to plan the auth-module hardening pass ``` Dry run inspects the repo and returns the Phase A-F plan without editing files, creating `.harness/`, running gates, or committing. To summarize an existing run: ``` Use gauntlet to show the harness status dashboard ``` --- ## How It Works

### The six-phase sequence | Phase | Name | What Happens | |-------|------|-------------| | **A** | Recon + Baseline | Scope the repo, read roadmap and CI config, run the full build and test suite, record exact counts. Write `.harness/feature-list.json` and `progress.md`. | | **B** | Audit Wave | 5-7 parallel auditors across dimensions (algorithmic correctness, concurrency/safety, API+doc accuracy, test quality, CI/tooling, portfolio presentation). Every medium+ finding goes through 2 adversarial verifiers (a 3rd on a split). Confirmed backlog saved to `.harness/`. | | **C** | Fix Waves | Critical/high issues first (orchestrator may fix critical ones inline for precision), then file-disjoint fixer clusters + judges. Gate. Commit at verified checkpoints. | | **D** | Build Wave | Remaining roadmap features, each with design-doc discipline. Acceptance bounds asserted in tests (assert, don't print). Judges verify. Gate. Commit. | | **E** | Docs Wave | Writers + dual-lens judges running both lenses simultaneously: claim-by-claim accuracy AND visual/voice polish. Real output for visuals, honestly labeled. Gate. Commit. | | **F** | Final Loop | Full suite + lint + release build + warnings-as-errors + signoff panel. Fix blockers, repeat F until zero blockers. Finalize `.harness/`, final commit. | ### The gated loop Each phase ends with a gate. The gate is the CI invocation, run verbatim from a clean checkout - never a filtered subset of tests, never just the new test classes. The orchestrator logs every iteration to `progress.md` (append-only) and does not move to the next phase until the gate is clean. The final signoff panel adds a human-quality check: three read-only reviewers, each with veto power, before declaring done. ### Bundled roadmap features - **Stack-specific auditor profiles**: Python, Swift, TypeScript, and Rust profiles ship in the skill bundle and are loaded only when Phase A detects the matching stack. - **Dry-run mode**: `--dry-run` or "plan only" produces the phase plan without mutating the repo. - **Harness state viewer**: `scripts/harness_state_view.py` renders `.harness/feature-list.json`, `progress.md`, and `audit-backlog.md` as a compact Markdown or JSON dashboard. --- ## Case Study The methodology has run on real projects, including **[ProximaKit](https://github.com/vivekptnk/ProximaKit)** (public) and a private, in-progress MLX port (described generically below until it ships). The clearest proof the gate discipline matters comes from that MLX port: a PyTorch-free port of a PyTorch imitation-learning policy for Apple Silicon, with numerical parity verified against the PyTorch reference. All local tests passed. The gate still caught four defect classes that ordinary local runs missed entirely. **What the gate caught that "all green" locally missed:** 1. A `.gitignore` rule silently excluded an entire source package from commits. Working tree: green. Clean checkout or CI: broken. Caught by clean-clone discipline - working-tree-green is not the same as checkout-green. 2. A hidden transitive dependency (`pandas`, pulled in via `pyarrow.Table.to_pandas`) that passed locally only because a dev-only extra had pulled pandas into the environment. Failed in a clean CI environment. Caught by CI plus a new subprocess test that blocks the import at the boundary. 3. A YAML 1.1 float trap: `'1e-05'` parses as a **string** in PyYAML, not a float. Would have silently poisoned the trainer's learning rate. Caught by a truthfulness judge diffing the generated config against the installed reference. 4. A train-time-only model bug: the ported attention had no dropout - invisible to every passing numerical-parity test (all run in eval mode) but would corrupt training dynamics. Caught by an architecture-fidelity judge reading the port against the reference source side-by-side. **What the harness confirmed:** numerical parity to the PyTorch reference was verified to ~1e-6 (end-to-end results ~430× inside the tolerance bound, comfortably within spec). The gate held the bar. Full story: [docs/CASE-STUDY.md](docs/CASE-STUDY.md) --- ## Lineage / Credits gauntlet composes three published methodologies into a gated generator-evaluator loop: - **[Anthropic - Building Effective AI Agents](https://www.anthropic.com/research/building-effective-agents)**: the evaluator-optimizer and orchestrator-workers workflow patterns that underpin the generator/evaluator separation and the multi-phase loop structure. - **[Anthropic - How we built our multi-agent research system](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/multi-agent-research-system)**: lead-agent/subagent orchestration and adversarial verification - the skeptical-verifier discipline (2+ independent REFUTE prompts per finding) comes directly from this. - **[Geoffrey Huntley - Ralph](https://ghuntley.com/ralph/)**: the external-state next-task → prompt → validate → log → repeat loop. gauntlet's `.harness/` directory and `progress.md` append-only log are the direct embodiment of this pattern. gauntlet is an independent open-source methodology. It is not affiliated with or endorsed by Anthropic. --- ## Roadmap | Item | Status | |------|--------| | Core harness skill (`/gauntlet` in Claude Code, `gauntlet` in Codex) | Shipped | | Bootstrap prompt (zero-install path) | Shipped | | Claude Code install target | Shipped | | Codex install target | Shipped | | Stack-specific auditor profiles (Python, Swift, TypeScript, Rust) | Shipped | | `--dry-run` mode: produce the phase plan without executing | Shipped | | Harness state viewer (render `.harness/` as a status dashboard) | Shipped | --- ## License MIT - use it, fork it, run it on anything. **Author:** [Vivek Pattanaik](https://github.com/vivekptnk)
